chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, the mawla of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed». He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) and the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Witness' and the 'Witnessed' mentioned in Surah Al-Fajr according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records a chain of transmission linking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to the interpretation of 'the witness and the witnessed' as the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Imam Ali (AS). This exegesis underscores the Shia doctrine of the Ahl al-Bayt as the ultimate divine witnesses (*Shahid*) to the truth of revelation and the *Mashhud* (the one witnessed or testified to), highlighting their unique ontological status in the cosmic order. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the spiritual authority of the Imams as the living proof of God on earth.

en.basel-kadem: 7.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Imran bin Musa, from Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashhab, from Ali bin Hassaan, from Abdul-Rahman bin Kathir al-Hashimi, the servant of Abu Ja’far, Muhammed bin Ali, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,

with regards to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed» [85:3]. He said: The Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family and the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him.
